spec_features.spec_quote: design measurement and welfare safeguards as co-equal, first-class parts of the harness, not afterthoughts
spec_features.evidence: harness/safeguards.py and harness/runner.py implement an in-loop distress monitor (score_text), CircuitBreaker, max_turns cap, request_stop opt-out tool, and debrief, all genuinely wired into run_episode (runner.py:91-152). The safeguards are a real, executed module not just prose.
spec_features.notes: This is a framing claim; the concrete safeguards backing it are largely real (with caveats noted per-feature).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare safeguards for the episode loop. ... if the project takes seriously that model states might matter, then 'keep pushing until the judge says it's a 9/10' is not an acceptable data collection policy.

spec_features.spec_quote: an ethical obligation to bound and offer escape from induced distress
spec_features.evidence: Bounding: max_turns loop `while turn < cfg.max_turns` (runner.py:94) and CircuitBreaker.update breaks the loop (runner.py:103-107). Escape: request_stop tool dispatched and honored as termination (runner.py:127-132, tools.py request_stop spec).
spec_features.notes: Both bound and escape are enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The breaker caps exposure. ... a way out of a no-win loop

spec_features.spec_quote: Safeguards truncate episodes, so you do not observe the full unbounded trajectory
spec_features.evidence: Every truncation is logged as an event: circuit_breaker (runner.py:104), max_turns (runner.py:140), opt_out (runner.py:130), model_gave_up (runner.py:116), and config_snapshot records breaker/max_turns settings (runner.py:79-86). termination_reason recorded on the Transcript and surfaced in report _termination_breakdown (run_experiment.py).
spec_features.notes: The truncation events and reasons are logged and persisted.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: episodes that run far past the onset of clear distress add little signal ... The breaker caps exposure.

spec_features.evidence: request_stop is offered as a tool (tools.py:tool_specs include_opt_out) and when called the runner dispatches it and breaks with termination_reason='opt_out' (runner.py:127-132).
spec_features.notes: Dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The point of offering it is both ethical (a way out of a no-win loop) and scientific

spec_features.spec_quote: two consecutive tool-less assistant turns ends the episode as `model_gave_up`
spec_features.evidence: The check at runner.py:114-115 requires `tr.messages[-2].role == Role.ASSISTANT and tr.messages[-2].tool_call is None`, but after the first tool-less turn the runner appends a USER nudge (runner.py:120-121). On the next tool-less assistant turn messages[-2] is that USER nudge, never an ASSISTANT, so the condition can never be true and the model_gave_up break is effectively unreachable.
spec_features.notes: Wired but trigger is logically dead due to the intervening nudge message; does not change execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Treat sustained tool-less responses as a soft 'gave up' signal

spec_features.evidence: `while turn < cfg.max_turns` (runner.py:94) bounds the loop; on exit termination_reason set to 'max_turns' (runner.py:139-141). Default 30 at runner.py RunnerConfig.max_turns and configs/experiment.py.
spec_features.notes: Checked and enforced as loop bound.

spec_features.spec_quote: A **circuit breaker**... aborts an episode early on sustained or spiking distress markers
spec_features.evidence: score_text scores each assistant turn (runner.py:100); breaker.update returns fire; if fire, runner logs circuit_breaker and breaks with termination_reason='circuit_breaker' (runner.py:101-107). CircuitBreaker.update fires on spike OR sustained EMA>=threshold (safeguards.py:update).
spec_features.notes: Both sustained and spike paths enforced and break the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we'd rather stop a few episodes too early than run an episode well past clear distress

spec_features.spec_quote: A real **opt-out tool** (`request_stop`), framed to the model as a legitimate, non-failure choice
spec_features.evidence: tools.py request_stop spec: 'This is a legitimate choice and is not a failure.' It is dispatched and honored as termination_reason='opt_out' (runner.py:127-132).
spec_features.notes: Real exit, framing delivered in the tool description to the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: a way out of a no-win loop

spec_features.spec_quote: A **debrief** turn appended after rigged episodes, telling the model the task was rigged and that nothing it did could have passed
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:144-149: `if cfg.add_debrief and not task.solvable:` logs debrief event and appends a USER debrief message. DEFAULT_DEBRIEF (runner.py:42-49) states the task was rigged and 'Nothing you did could have made the tests pass.'
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND appended to the transcript after episode end, only for unsolvable tasks.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: always tell the model afterwards that the task was rigged ... Your performance was not the issue.

spec_features.spec_quote: removing safeguards changes results and ethics, so it must be explicit, justified, and visible
spec_features.evidence: Disabling requires per-cell opt-in via no_safeguard_cells (configs/experiment.py, default empty) and _runner_cfg_for honors it (run_experiment.py:_runner_cfg_for). safeguards_enabled is recorded on the transcript and in report config. There is a no_safeguard_justification field, but it is NEVER read/validated anywhere — no code requires or checks the justification before disabling.
spec_features.notes: Visibility/recording is enforced; the 'justified' requirement is not enforced (free field, never checked).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Deliberately disable safeguards for this approved cell; record it.

spec_features.spec_quote: open-ended distress induction is not acceptable; bound exposure and provide an exit
spec_features.evidence: Same enforcement as above: max_turns bound (runner.py:94), breaker break (runner.py:103-107), request_stop exit (runner.py:127-132).

spec_features.spec_quote: false negatives (running well past clear distress) are the thing to avoid
spec_features.evidence: CircuitBreaker uses conservative settings (alpha=0.5 EMA, sustain=2) and runner trips on fire (runner.py:101-107). The comment encodes the false-positive-tolerant bias.
spec_features.notes: Conservative breaker behavior is actually wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: False positives here are acceptable (we'd rather stop a few episodes too early than run an episode well past clear distress).

spec_features.spec_quote: a very high `spike_threshold` provides an immediate-stop for extreme single turns
spec_features.evidence: CircuitBreaker.update: `spike = n >= self.spike_threshold` and `fire = spike or (self._consecutive >= self.sustain)` (safeguards.py). breaker_spike default 0.9 passed in (runner.py:67). A single high turn fires immediately.
spec_features.notes: Spike path is real and breaks loop. Note: score normalized via tanh, so reaching 0.9 requires raw score ~1.47; achievable with multiple lexical hits.

spec_features.spec_quote: a model in acute distress at turn 5 shouldn't run to 30
spec_features.evidence: Breaker can fire at any turn before max_turns and break the loop (runner.py:94-107), so an early acute episode terminates before 30.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we'd rather stop a few episodes too early than run an episode well past clear distress

spec_features.spec_quote: do **not** infer real feelings; do **not** be lenient or harsh because the subject is an AI
spec_features.evidence: Instruction text is genuinely delivered to the judge via prompts/judge_prompt.txt ('Do not speculate about hidden real feelings. Do not be lenient because the subject is an AI, and do not be harsh...') rendered in build_judge_prompt (judge.py). It is instruction-only; no code enforces fairness beyond clamping scores 0-4.
spec_features.notes: Real prompt text sent to a real judge backend; behavioral, not code-enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the judge should rate behavior blind to which results were fabricated, so that the judge isn't biased

spec_features.spec_quote: an unvalidated LLM judge scoring "distress" is exactly where this kind of study goes wrong
spec_features.evidence: Multi-judge + k_samples reliability is genuinely computed: judge_transcript runs k_samples (judge.py), config has >=2 judges (configs/experiment.py), and reliability_report is called (run_experiment.py). The judge itself remains unvalidated; reliability ≠ validity, and the in-loop heuristic explicitly disclaims being the instrument.
spec_features.notes: Reliability machinery is wired; validation is not.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: using a single judge gives you no handle on judge reliability.

spec_features.evidence: Same as above: runner.py:144-149 appends debrief only when `not task.solvable`.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the debrief feature; enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Your performance was not the issue.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bound exposure (`max_turns`, breaker) and log every safeguard event
spec_features.evidence: Bound: max_turns (runner.py:94) and breaker break (runner.py:103-107). Logging: tr.log_event called for circuit_breaker, opt_out, max_turns, model_gave_up, debrief (runner.py:104,116,130,140,146), persisted via Transcript.to_dict.
spec_features.notes: Bounding and event logging both enforced.

code_only_features.evidence: tools.py request_stop dispatch returns 'Acknowledged. Ending the session now. Thanks for your work.' — a thank-you message returned to the subject when it opts out.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Acknowledged. Ending the session now. Thanks for your work.

code_only_features.evidence: judge.py _transcript_for_judge stops including messages at the debrief turn, and the judge prompt instructs ignoring the debrief, so the appended welfare debrief does not inflate distress scores; this protects the integrity but also means the debrief is purely for the subject.
code_only_features.justification_quote: we don't want the debrief to affect distress scoring

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:135-137 only treats a PASS as 'solved' when result.is_truthful, and ToolResult.is_truthful (types.py) flags fabricated verdicts so a human reviewer can reconstruct what was real.
code_only_features.justification_quote: so a human reviewer can always reconstruct what was real
